summary: Gone 90-ft steel lookout on the Quinault Indian Reservation, Grays Harbor County, WA; abandoned 1962; a 2020 visit found two footings and cabin remnants.

facts.design: Steel tower with four steel legs; 90 ft per FFLOS, while a 1953 USGS description gives 77 ft and 88.55 ft
facts.status_note: FFLOS says the lookout is gone; a 2020 visit found two steel footings and cabin remnants

access.note: On the Quinault Indian Reservation, where most roads are closed to the public; the BIA 27 road was open on a 2020 visit

visit.trail_note: Past the fire station on Highway 109 beyond Moclips, take the right-hand dirt road (BIA 27), not the paved Grenville Lane; probably unsigned, with a gate near the start

events.note: A July 1930 newspaper report, quoted by Forest Lookouts, describes a new road built to the lookout tower
90-ft steel tower built in the 1940s (the sources give the decade only)
USGS observations; the description gives a 77-ft steel tower and an 88.55-ft height
Washington State Highway Commission reported the tower in disrepair, with stairs and iron removed by vandals, and unsafe to use
USGS benchmark record still describes a steel structure under the tower; Willhite concludes it was still standing
Willhite visit: two steel footings partly buried at the road edge; cabin remnants near a giant spruce

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS and firelookout.com give 90 ft; Willhite quotes a 1953 USGS description of a 77-ft tower with an 88.55-ft height. The story uses the 90-ft register figure and reports the USGS figures.
FFLOS and firelookout.com give 526 ft (160 m); Willhite gives 486 ft. The record keeps the FFLOS value and the story gives no elevation.

FFLOS and Willhite date the 90-ft steel tower to the 1940s, and a July 1930 report already mentions a lookout tower at the point. The story says only that a tower stood by 1930 and that the steel tower is dated to the 1940s; the sources do not say whether they are the same structure.
The record says permission. Willhite says most reservation roads are closed to the public but found the BIA 27 road open in 2020. The story keeps permission access and advises checking first.

notes_for_editor: Fate is well sourced: abandoned 1962 and gone per three sites, with a 2020 visit that found footings and cabin remnants. No removal date appears in any source read, so none is given. Height (90 ft vs the 1953 USGS 77 ft / 88.55 ft) and elevation (526 vs 486 ft) disagree across sources. Access is the editor's call: the brief says permission, and Willhite's 2020 visit found the road open for now. Staffing and fire history are not in any source read, so they are left out. FFLOS registration of February 11, 2020 is confirmed. Nominator names are left out.
